admission.workflow: Real Institution readiness, system-browser approval, native signing custody, Session rotation, and a credential-free authenticated window handoff.

items.rationale: Preserved Microsoft MIT attribution for the reviewed cluster.

Retains ephemeral IPv4 binding, asynchronous start/result/stop, startup deadline and state-bound callback lifecycle. Proctor requires a random exact single route, constant-time independent state validation, one-use completion, cancellation, bounded requests/connections and idempotent bounded shutdown. GitHub signin redirect, arbitrary static files, portable environment and custom VS Code activation are explicitly excluded.

Preserves ephemeral startup, missing callback parameters and successful state/code completion tests through the Proctor interface. Upstream signin redirect and callback-to-static-page redirect assertions are excluded with those routes. Adds wrong Host, duplicate state, replay, cancellation and deadline checks.

The loopback caller supplies PKCE S256, a five-minute deadline, cancellation and finally cleanup. Other provider flows, device-code and manual fallback, provider login/account selection, extension telemetry/progress and GitHub exchange endpoints are excluded. Proctor consumes its server contract and opens only the returned same-origin hosted URL.

Electron main safeStorage availability/encrypt/decrypt informs OS-encrypted refresh persistence. The generic service, command-line plaintext backend, buffer JSON representation and raw error logging are excluded. Native signing custody is independent, and never serializes a private key.

dependencies.reference: Node.js HTTP, URL, crypto, timers and filesystem APIs
dependencies.rationale: Pinned Node/Electron APIs supply ephemeral loopback transport, bounded parsing, PKCE and atomic encrypted file replacement; no runtime upstream checkout.
Only main opens the server-returned hosted URL and encrypts refresh storage. No plaintext backend or renderer credentials.
Accepted cancellation and disposable ownership fence listener, network, and Session effects.
Native macOS Security.framework and Windows CNG key references supply P-256 signing and public JWK access with private export disabled.

divergences.summary: Server-hosted authentication method choice and explicit approval replace provider-specific extensions. Exact callback state/path, PKCE, DPoP nonce challenges and no ambiguous one-use retry strengthen the transport. There is no local static file host, signin redirect, custom protocol, provider API or copyable-code fallback.

Development and production both require non-exportable OS key custody; only public keys and signatures leave the native adapter. Refresh credentials alone use OS encryption, with a durable rotation-pending barrier. Access credentials remain in main memory and only validated public identity enters the renderer. Windows implementation still requires target-native conformance before a supported release claim.

verification.obligation: Exercise exact loopback, state validation, replay, cancellation, deadlines, PKCE, DPoP, nonce retry, ambiguous refresh fencing, and sign-out during a pending write.
On the target OS, verify real native signing/key persistence, OS-encrypted refresh storage, credential-free sandboxed authenticated renderer and sign-out.
Validate schema, path ownership, attribution and verification offline.
Verify every pinned upstream path/blob and review declared behavior divergences.
